topic: May 2026 OFAC Operation Economic Fury Iran shadow-banking designations
jurisdiction: US (OFAC); secondary regulatory implications EU, UK, HK, UAE

claims.claim: On May 1, 2026, OFAC designated 35 entities and individuals tied to Iran's shadow-banking architecture under Operation Economic Fury.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Treasury — Press Release SB-0477: Economic Fury Targets Iran Shadow Banking Facilitators
supports: Number of designated entities and individuals (35)
limits: Press release; the operative legal action is the corresponding SDN list update
Designations and general licenses can be amended; verify against current OFAC list before operational use

sources.name: Investing.com / Reuters — US Treasury sanctions 35 entities in Iran shadow banking crackdown
limits: Secondary reporting; cite the Treasury press release as the primary source for any operational decision

claims.claim: OFAC explicitly identifies the Zarringhalam network's front companies in Hong Kong and the UAE as a primary mechanism for cover-company transactions on behalf of Iranian entities.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Treasury — Press Release SB-0477
supports: Naming of Hong Kong and the UAE as preferred shell-company jurisdictions
Stated rationale that these jurisdictions are 'easy to establish and subject to less scrutiny'
limits: Characterization is from the Treasury press release; jurisdictions named have their own enforcement frameworks

sources.name: Arab News — US Treasury warns UAE, Hong Kong banks over Iran-linked money flows
supports: Regulatory-attention framing toward UAE and HK banks
limits: Secondary reporting; framing reflects journalistic interpretation

claims.claim: The May 2026 action builds on a January 15, 2026 OFAC shadow-banking action targeting 'rahbar' networks of Bank Melli and Shahr Bank.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Treasury — Press Release SB-0477 (references the prior January 15, 2026 action)
supports: Existence and date of prior January 15 action
Targets of prior action (Bank Melli, Shahr Bank rahbar networks)
limits: Primary text of the January 15 action requires separate retrieval

claims.claim: EU and UK regulators are likely to update typology-based supervisory expectations in response to OFAC's typology disclosure within 1–2 quarters.
Correspondent-banking partners in HK and the UAE will tighten internal KYC documentation requests independently and visibly, increasing operational friction even on legitimate flows.
